opening.headline: It is convenient to have AI directly view and process emails, calendars, and documents, but how much it shows and how much is left to you is determined by your authority.
body: To schedule a meeting, you alternate between opening an email thread, calendar, and shared document and pasting the content into an AI conversation window. In the process, it's easy to lose track of updates or miss someone's schedule. It would be much more convenient if AI could directly open and process the app.

In this class, we will look at what the connector between AI and apps is, what permissions are requested when connecting, and how the risks of read and write/execute permissions differ. Next, we will check how the agent function, which carries out various steps on its own, operates on this structure and determine where to place the approval step in the case of meeting schedule coordination.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the role of connector and agent functions
You can distinguish the risk difference between read permission and write/execute permission.

screens.title: It would be nice if AI could directly read emails, calendars, and documents.
screens.lead: First, let's look at a troublesome scene that many people experience. Read the situation below and think about what makes you uncomfortable.

visual.alt: Illustration showing the flow of a user copying and pasting mail, calendar, and document contents one by one into the AI chat window.
labels: Schedule a team meeting for next week
Might I have missed some of the latest content?

paragraphs: We need to schedule a team meeting for next week. Candidate times are scattered across email threads, attendees' available times are on calendars, and agendas are written out in shared documents. To receive help from AI, you must open the contents of these three places one by one and paste them into the chat window.

It's easy to lose the latest reply or miss someone's schedule while copying and pasting. Since only the content at the time of pasting is transmitted to the AI, any changes made in the meantime are not reflected.

It would be much more convenient if AI could directly open and process these apps. However, opening it directly also means that AI has access to my mail and schedule. The core question of this lesson is this. How much will we show to AI, and how much will we leave to AI?

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Are reading emails and sending emails the same level of entrustment? By the end of class, you will be able to answer this question with evidence.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen why convenience is necessary, let's start by thinking about how I deliver information.

screens.title: How are you delivering information to AI now?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to type or submit your answer, so just think of it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Are you copying and pasting the content into the chat window?
items.answer: This is the most common method. Since people select the content, I can directly control the scope that AI sees. Instead, it takes effort to move it, and AI doesn't know if the original changes after pasting.

items.prompt: Are you uploading a file to read it?
items.answer: Uploading files is also a way for people to decide what to give. AI only sees files at the time they were uploaded. Since uploading a file grants access, the user is responsible for deciding which file to upload.

items.prompt: Are you connecting the app and letting the AI find it for you?
items.answer: This is the connector method we will cover in this class. Instead of eliminating human effort, the AI's access range is determined by authority when first connecting. As convenient as it is, I need to be aware of what I am allowing.

screens.outro: Now that we remember the difference between copy/upload and connection, let’s find out what a connector is.

screens.title: What is a Connector: A Pathway Between Apps and AI?
screens.lead: Hover over or select an underlined term in the description below to see a short description. Check the terms one by one.

visual.alt: An illustration showing an AI chat window connected to several apps through a connection line in the middle.

data.text: connector is a connection that allows AI to access a user's apps and services, retrieve data, and operate within those services. For example, in Claude's documentation, you can create an issue in Linear, send a message to Slack, or search files in Google Drive. OpenAI refers to the same concept as "connected apps" and explains that you can connect services like Google Drive or Slack to perform tasks such as file searching, document summarization, and message retrieval. Once Claude has connected an app, it can automatically use Introduce yourself into conversation when appropriate, eliminating the need to mention the app name each time. Additionally, if a remote server follows MCP, even if it is not listed in the default provided list, it can be connected via custom connector.

terms.tip: This is a connection that allows AI to retrieve data from apps and services and even perform actions within those services. OpenAI calls them Connected apps.
An open standard protocol for AI apps to connect to external tools and data. AI apps can connect to any server that follows the rules in the same way.

This is a method of directly connecting services that are not in the default list. You add it by pointing to a remote MCP server and use shared credentials to access everything those credentials reach.
If Claude determines that a linked app is helpful to a question, Claude uses that app without the user having to say the name of the app.

screens.outro: Now that we have an idea of what a connection is, let's take a look at what permissions actually appear on the screen when you connect.

screens.title: List of permissions requested on the connection screen
screens.lead: During the connection process, users review and approve services and permissions. In the table below, compare how read items and write/execute items are divided by service.

visual.alt: In the connector connection dialog box, permission items are lined up, with read and write color-coded.

data.caption: Nature of request rights and risks for each service
columns: a movement that is difficult to reverse
rows: Search and read mail in natural language, view draft lists in drafts, and view metadata in attachments.
Send, reply, and forward messages are difficult to retrieve once they are sent out. Claude will by default ask for permission before running.
View events and shared calendars, find possible overlapping times for attendees
Create/edit/delete schedule, manage attendees, respond to invitations, set up recurring meetings
Deleting events and sending invitations will immediately affect other attendees.
Search and import Google Docs, view file metadata, view file permissions and recent changes list
Create folders, upload files, save files created by Claude, share/move/send to trash
Share, Move, and Recycle Bin are basically actions that ask for approval before execution.
Data inquiry within the range permitted by the service
Changes to the scope permitted by the Service
When you use shared credentials, you access everything that the credential touches, so you need to check scopes separately.
data.notes: Claude inherits the same permissions that each person has on the connected service. Even connectors cannot reach files or channels that were originally unviewable. The connection sequence involves selecting an app, logging into your account, reviewing and approving the requested services and permissions.

screens.outro: Now that we've divided permissions into read and write, let's compare how the two types of risks differ.

screens.title: Read permission and write/execute permission have different risks.
screens.lead: Switch between the two states to compare possible behavior in the same mail app and the impact of a problem.

states.label: read
states.body: This is an action to search mail and view schedule. Data inside the app does not change or go out. However, since what you read is posted in conversations, you must consider the issue of sensitive information being exposed in conversations separately. The risk of read access is primarily a matter of what is visible: exposure. If you focus on reading, even if you make a mistake, you can usually reverse it.

states.label: Write/Execute
states.body: An action that changes the state of a service, such as sending an email, deleting a schedule, or posting a message. Once it happens, it is difficult to reverse or affects others. So, by default, Claude's Gmail connection asks for user approval before sending, replying, or forwarding, and on Team and Enterprise plans, the owner decides whether to allow it to run without approval. In this way, the stage where a human confirms before execution is the approval stage. OpenAI's admin documentation also covers different controls for installing plugins, accessing the app, and what the app does.

screens.outro: Now that we have distinguished the differences in risk, let us see how the agent function operates on this structure.

screens.title: Agent functionality: self-executes multiple steps in succession
screens.lead: Let's follow the flow of an agent processing a single request step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

visual.alt: An illustration showing the five steps an agent goes through in a horizontal timeline below one line of a request.
labels: Schedule a team meeting next week and guide me through it.

steps.title: make a plan
steps.body: The agent function does not end with a single answer, but plans several steps of action on its own. All the user needs to do is describe the task. ChatGPT's agent mode documentation notes that once you describe the task, the agent starts executing it.

steps.title: Read in app
steps.body: Depending on your plan, connected apps will read the information you need. This step is done with read permission. The document advises agents to be very careful about accessing sensitive information when using apps as a data source.

steps.title: Create a draft
steps.body: Create a draft schedule or email draft based on what you read. The draft doesn't go to anyone yet, so this step is a preparatory step that doesn't change its status.

steps.title: Confirmation request
steps.body: The agent stops when necessary and asks for confirmation or clarification from the user. Users can change direction or interrupt progress. The document explains that there are user-verified safeguards in place for high-impact actions, but it does not eliminate all risks, so it advises to use them cautiously.

steps.title: Run and Repeat
steps.body: Once approved, write operations such as creating a schedule or sending an email are performed. ChatGPT Workspace Agents creates agents for these recurring tasks to connect apps and tools, share them with your team, and run them on a schedule. Agents can only be viewed and run by authorized people, and administrators can turn them on or off by default. Please note that the ChatGPT agent documentation indicates that this mode is no longer available, and that long, multi-step tasks should use ChatGPT Work.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the agent flow and verification steps, let's apply it to a real-world example.

screens.title: Commentary: Breaking down meeting scheduling into steps
screens.lead: The instructor divides the meeting schedule coordination request into a reading phase and a writing phase. Select the right arrow to see the steps one by one.

steps.title: Confirm request
steps.body: My request is to schedule a team meeting next week and inform attendees. In this one sentence, viewing the app and changing the app are mixed together. The starting point for judgment is to first determine which part is reading and which part is writing.

steps.title: Step 1 Reading: Mail Thread
steps.body: Find candidate times and requests in relevant mail threads. Since the task is to read emails, read permission is sufficient. If you make a mistake at this step, your mail will not be sent or deleted.

steps.title: Step 2 Reading: Calendar
steps.body: Check your calendar for attendees' available times. This too is reading. Because each person only inherits the permissions they have in the connected service, you may not see the schedules of attendees you cannot see.

steps.title: Step 3: Preparing to Write: Draft
steps.body: Create a draft meeting schedule and draft information email. The draft doesn't go to anyone yet, so it doesn't have any external impact. This is where a person can review the content.

steps.title: Step 4: Write: Execute
steps.body: Creating events and sending emails are actions that directly affect other people. Leave the approval step to run only when a person has checked and approved the draft.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: Steps 1 and 2, which only require reading, are not risky if left broadly. It is safer to leave approval for step 4. If you break it down into steps instead of doing it all at once, it becomes clear where to place human confirmation.

screens.outro: This time, let's compare the same task with scope of authority.

screens.title: Commentary: Doing the same thing with narrower authority
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare the results of the same error when connected with broad and narrow permissions.

tabs.label: wide authority
tabs.body: In addition to reading all emails, you can also open sending and deleting them. It may seem convenient, but if the AI ​​misinterprets the request or is fooled by malicious content, a single error can lead to immediate outsourcing or deletion. The ChatGPT agent document also explains that agents connected to the app can access sensitive data such as emails or files and act on behalf of the user, resulting in risks such as prompt injection.

tabs.label: narrow authority
tabs.body: The connection is based on reading, and sending is done by creating a draft and sending it directly to a person. Even if the same error occurs, the damage stops at the draft level, giving people time to correct the content before sending it out. Even if there is an approval step, it only makes sense if a person actually reads and verifies the content. The rule is to open only the steps necessary for work and give approval for steps that are difficult to reverse.

tabs.label: Administrator Perspective
tabs.body: In organizations, managers also reduce scope. ChatGPT Enterprise·Edu has new plugins and apps disabled by default, and Business has them enabled by default. Administrators coordinate availability in their organizations. Installing plugins and accessing apps within them are evaluated as separate controls. Claude's Team and Enterprise plans also require owners to first turn on the connector at the organization level before individual users can authenticate.

screens.outro: Since I have explained the perspective of reducing authority, I will summarize the content so far.

screens.title: Key Takeaway: The more connected you are, the more convenient it is, but also the more authority you have.
screens.lead: We summarize the key points of this class in one place. Read the information below in order and answer the first question.

paragraphs: A connector is a passage through which AI retrieves app data and operates within the service, and the agent function uses this passage in several stages. Connecting eliminates the effort of copying and pasting, but the scope that AI can access and change is determined by authority.

The risk of read permissions is closer to exposure, while the risk of write/execute permissions is closer to changes that are difficult to reverse. So, to the first question, whether reading and sending emails are the same level of entrustment, the answer is no. Reading can be wide open, but sending leaves the approval step.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: We open permissions only to the level necessary for work, and require human confirmation before actions that are difficult to reverse. In organizations, administrators can further narrow the scope of apps and tasks.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: What is the biggest reason why drafting and sending mail are treated as different permissions in the mail connection?
options: This is because once it happens, it is difficult to reverse and affects other people.
This is because drafting is a much slower process than sending.
If you have read permission, sending permission is automatically included.
This is because the draft cannot contain any sensitive information.
checks.explain: Writing/executing is handled separately from reading because it is difficult to return once it goes out and affects others, and an approval step is placed before sending.

wrong.1: The criterion for dividing power is not speed, but the reversibility and impact of the results.
wrong.2: Read and Write/Execute are separate permission items and do not follow automatically.
wrong.3: Drafts can also contain content that has been read, so there are no issues with sensitive information.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded. Try placing items in a safe disposition order.
checks.q: Put the steps in the right order to safely handle meeting scheduling requests.
items: Find candidate times and requests in relevant mail threads
Check attendees' available times on your calendar
Create a draft schedule and a draft guidance email
Once a person checks and approves the contents, create a schedule and send an email.
checks.explain: The reading phase gathers information, creates a draft that doesn't go to anyone yet, and then the difficult-to-reverse writing phase occurs only after human approval.

glossary.def: This is a connection that allows AI to access the user's apps and services, retrieve data, and even perform actions within those services.
This is a function that allows you to plan multiple tasks on your own and continue carrying them out using connected apps and tools.
Read is the right to view data, and Write/Execute is the right to change the status of the service, such as sending mail or changing the schedule.
This is the step where the user confirms and allows the contents before writing or executing.
An open standard protocol for AI apps to connect to external tools and data.

misconceptions.myth: When you connect the app, AI can see all information in your account.
misconceptions.fact: Claude inherits the same permissions that each person has on the connected service. You cannot reach files or channels that were originally unviewable. However, custom connectors that use shared credentials access anywhere those credentials can reach.

misconceptions.myth: There is absolutely no risk if you just read it.
misconceptions.fact: Reading doesn't change your data, but you still need to consider exposing sensitive information because what you read will end up in conversations.

misconceptions.myth: Once the connector is turned on, the human work is done.
misconceptions.fact: It is safer to leave human approval before writing and execution. Agent safeguards do not eliminate all risks and must be used with caution.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: The more connected you are, the more convenient it becomes, but also the more power you have.
Reading is a matter of exposure, while writing/execution is a matter of changes that are difficult to reverse.
The acknowledgment step is a human confirmation device that precedes an action that is difficult to reverse.
Open permissions only to the level necessary for your work.
closing.reflectionLead: Now think for yourself. This question will not be submitted or graded, and there is no space to enter an answer.
closing.reflection: What steps in my job should AI not perform directly?
